headline: Deep sequence models predict gene expression, splicing and variant effects
label: Deep Learning Genomic Sequence Models
summary: Sequence-to-function models are now being extended to personal genomes, tumor promoter variants, and multi-tissue TWAS fine-mapping.
synthesis: The dominant thread is supervised and generative deep learning that links DNA and RNA sequence to molecular readouts. Decima predicts cell type-specific expression from sequence, trained on single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq from over 22 million cells. Evo2 delta scores prioritize promoter variants across about 1,250 CRC genes and are validated against GWAS. Fine-tuning Enformer on paired personal genome and transcriptome data improves held-out individuals but not unseen contexts. TrASPr+BOS couples a transformer with Bayesian optimization to predict and design tissue-specific splicing, and an XGBoost model with SHAP extracts RBP regulatory logic for exon skipping. Statistical genetics work, including bsBSLMM, mFABIO and multi-ancestry TWAS, extends association-based prioritization of causal genes. What is new relative to predictive accuracy is attention to transfer limits, interpretability, and design, along with NAT interaction scores that track clinical stage in CRC.
